items.prompt: Cybersecurity objectives are linked to business mission, critical services and stakeholder needs.
items.recommended_action: Document the outcomes cybersecurity must protect and who depends on them.

items.prompt: Cybersecurity roles, decision rights and risk ownership are explicit.
items.recommended_action: Assign accountable owners and define who may accept material cyber risk.

items.prompt: Leadership defines or approves cybersecurity risk tolerance and priorities.
items.recommended_action: Record risk tolerance and use it to resolve competing decisions.

items.prompt: Material cybersecurity policies are implemented, reviewed and tied to accountable owners.
items.recommended_action: For each policy identify owner, implementation evidence and review date.

items.prompt: Supplier and regulatory cyber obligations are identified and assigned to controls and owners.
items.recommended_action: Create an obligation and supplier-risk map linked to owners and evidence.

items.prompt: The organisation maintains an inventory of systems, services, devices and significant software dependencies.
items.recommended_action: Build a minimum viable inventory and identify assets supporting critical services.

items.prompt: Critical data and its locations, owners and sensitivity are known.
items.recommended_action: Identify critical data sets, owners, locations and handling requirements.

items.prompt: External dependencies and single points of failure are identified for critical services.
items.recommended_action: Map critical third parties, connectivity and platform dependencies to services.

items.prompt: Vulnerabilities and insecure configurations are discovered through defined processes.
items.recommended_action: Define how weaknesses are found, recorded and assigned.

items.prompt: Cyber risks are recorded with business impact, assumptions, owners and treatment decisions.
items.recommended_action: Use a risk register that distinguishes evidence, assumptions and treatment status.

items.prompt: Access to important systems follows least privilege and strong authentication.
items.recommended_action: Review privileged and remote access first; remove unnecessary rights.

items.prompt: Security updates and configuration baselines are managed for supported systems.
items.recommended_action: Define patch and configuration expectations by criticality and track exceptions.

items.prompt: Backups are protected from the same failure or compromise as production systems.
items.recommended_action: Separate critical backups and test them after a realistic compromise scenario.

items.prompt: Personnel receive role-appropriate cybersecurity guidance and training.
items.recommended_action: Prioritise high-risk roles and tie training to real workflows.

items.prompt: Sensitive data is protected in storage, transfer and disposal according to risk.
items.recommended_action: Define minimum protection rules and verify implementation.

items.prompt: Security-relevant logs exist for critical systems and are retained long enough to investigate incidents.
items.recommended_action: Identify the minimum logs needed to detect and reconstruct high-impact incidents.

items.prompt: Monitoring has defined owners, alert routes and response expectations.
items.recommended_action: Define receiver, response time and escalation for critical alert sources.

items.prompt: The organisation can recognise meaningful anomalies in critical services and identities.
items.recommended_action: Define high-value abnormal conditions and confirm they are detectable.

items.prompt: Detection includes material third-party and cloud signals where the organisation depends on them.
items.recommended_action: Identify supplier and cloud signals that must reach incident response.

items.prompt: Detection coverage is tested with realistic scenarios rather than assumed from tool deployment.
items.recommended_action: Run controlled detection tests and record expected versus observed alerts.

items.prompt: A usable incident-response plan defines roles, authority and escalation paths.
items.recommended_action: Build the plan around real decision rights and contact paths.

items.prompt: Internal, customer, supplier and regulatory communication responsibilities are defined before an incident.
items.recommended_action: Predefine communication owners, approval routes and required information.

items.prompt: The organisation can contain affected accounts, devices or services without improvising basic access.
items.recommended_action: Prepare and test containment actions for plausible high-impact incidents.

items.prompt: Incident evidence is preserved sufficiently for investigation, learning and required reporting.
items.recommended_action: Define minimum evidence-preservation steps before an incident occurs.

items.prompt: Exercises test real people, decisions and dependencies, not only the existence of a plan.
items.recommended_action: Run a scenario forcing escalation, containment, communication and supplier coordination.

items.prompt: Critical systems and data have tested recovery procedures.
items.recommended_action: Perform and retain evidence from an end-to-end recovery test.

items.prompt: Recovery priorities and time/data-loss objectives are defined from business needs.
items.recommended_action: Agree service recovery order and tolerable time/data loss with business owners.

items.prompt: Critical processes have a defined degraded or alternative operating mode.
items.recommended_action: Define the minimum viable service when normal systems are unavailable.

items.prompt: Recovery plans account for critical suppliers and external dependencies.
items.recommended_action: Test recovery when a critical supplier is unavailable or compromised.

items.prompt: Post-incident lessons produce owned improvements that are later verified.
items.recommended_action: Track lessons to owners, due dates and verification evidence.
